component.name: Checkbox
component.description: A single on/off choice with a visible text label, built on a native checkbox input so it submits with an ordinary HTML form. The whole row (box and label) is the click target. Supports uncontrolled (defaultChecked) and controlled (checked + onChange) use, and a disabled state whether checked or unchecked.

when: A single independent yes/no setting the user confirms with a form (notification preferences, terms acceptance)
Several independent options in a list where any combination can be chosen — one Checkbox per option
The choice is binary; use Select when choosing one value from a finite list

patterns.name: preference-list
patterns.description: A stack of independent notification preferences under a section heading inside a Card.

patterns.name: form-consent-row
patterns.description: A consent checkbox placed above the submit Button at the end of a form.
patterns.tree: Stack(gap=lg) > [TextField, Checkbox(label='I agree to the terms'), Button]

antiPatterns.scenario: Using Checkbox for mutually exclusive options
antiPatterns.reason: Checkboxes are independent; a group of them does not enforce a single choice.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use Select for choosing one value from a list.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using Checkbox as a filter toggle in a toolbar
antiPatterns.reason: Filter toggles are pressed-state buttons with their own visual language.

antiPatterns.scenario: Passing the label as children or wrapping Checkbox in an extra <label>
antiPatterns.reason: Checkbox already renders its own <label> around the input and the label Text; a second label nests labels and breaks the accessible name.
antiPatterns.alternative: Pass the visible text through the label prop; use hideLabel when the name must be assistive-technology only.

antiPatterns.scenario: Overriding the label color for the disabled state
antiPatterns.reason: The label renders through <Text>, which switches to color='disabled' automatically when disabled is set.
antiPatterns.alternative: Set disabled on the Checkbox and let it style the label.

purpose.false: Unchecked. Input background with a neutral input border.
purpose.true: Checked. Brand-filled box with an inverted check glyph. Controlled via checked + onChange, or seeded with defaultChecked.

states.description: Input background with a neutral input border.
Brand-filled box with an inverted check glyph. Set via checked (controlled) or defaultChecked (uncontrolled).
Stronger input border on the unchecked box while the pointer is anywhere over the row (box or label), matching the click target.
Disabled border, disabled label colour, not-allowed cursor; toggling blocked natively.
Disabled background fill with the inverted check glyph and disabled label colour.

accessibility.notes: Native <input type="checkbox"> restyled with appearance: none, wrapped in a <label> so the label text is both the accessible name and a click target. The check glyph is aria-hidden; checked state is conveyed natively. className lands on the root <label>; every other native attribute (id, name, value, style, aria-*) is forwarded to the input. No id is generated — the wrapping label associates the name.
